chunks: And it is narrated from al-Walīd ibn Ṣabīḥ, who said:

I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام when a beggar came to him, and he gave him. Then another came, and he gave him. Then another came, and he gave him. Then another came, and he said, “May Allah grant you abundance.”

Then he said, “Indeed, if a man had wealth reaching thirty or forty thousand dirhams, then wished to leave nothing of it except that he placed it in a rightful cause, he would do so, and then remain with no wealth. Thus he would be among the three whose supplication is rejected.”

He said: I said, “Who are they?” He said, “One of them is a man who had wealth, then spent it in other than its proper way, then said: ‘My Lord, provide for me,’ and the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘Did I not provide for you?’ And a man who sat in his house and does not strive in seeking sustenance, yet says: ‘My Lord, provide for me,’ and the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘Did I not make for you a way to seek sustenance?’ And a man who has a wife who harms him, so he says: ‘My Lord, deliver me from her,’ and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘Did I not place her affair in your hand?’”

key_terms.تُؤْذِيهِ: she causes him harm or distress
key_terms.سَائِلٌ: a beggar or petitioner asking for assistance
key_terms.سَبِيلًا: a means or path made available for action
key_terms.فِي حَقٍّ: in a rightful and proper cause
key_terms.مَالٌ: wealth or property possessed by a person
key_terms.يُرَدُّ دُعَاؤُهُمْ: their supplication is turned back and not answered
key_terms.ٱلرِّزْقِ: sustenance or provision granted by Allah

ai.seo_question: Whose supplication does Allah reject according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that charity and spending in rightful causes must be balanced with responsibility and sound judgment. It also teaches that du'a is not accepted from one who neglects the means Allah has already given him in wealth, livelihood, or resolving his family affairs.
